question.0c: My mind goes blank and I can't say anything

question.1: When you're treated unfairly at work, what's your pattern?
question.1a: I express my anger and immediately raise the issue
question.1b: I start browsing job sites or throw myself into other work
question.1c: I go numb and think 'that's just how it is'
question.1d: I try to understand my boss's position and work even harder
question.2: When you find out a close friend shared your secret with others?
question.2a: I confront them directly and firmly
question.2b: I cut contact and create distance
question.2c: I feel betrayed and freeze, unable to do anything
question.2d: I rationalize that they must have had a good reason
question.3: Right before an important deadline, an unexpected problem arises?
question.3a: I pour all my energy into finding and fixing the cause
question.3b: I handle other urgent tasks first, avoiding the real problem
question.3c: I panic and nothing seems manageable
question.3d: I ask everyone around for help and follow their suggestions
question.4: Your partner suddenly says 'we need to talk.' Your reaction?
question.4a: I get defensive — 'What did I do wrong?'
question.4b: Anxiety hits and I start running worst-case scenarios in my head
question.4c: My emotions shut down and I just sit there blankly
question.4d: I immediately say 'I'll change, what do you want?'
question.5: Late at night, a bad memory suddenly surfaces. What do you do?
question.5a: Anger rises and I punch a pillow or exercise
question.5b: I turn on Netflix or scroll social media to escape
question.5c: My body freezes and I just stare at the ceiling
question.5d: I text someone and start a casual conversation pretending I'm fine
question.6: You make a mistake in front of a crowd. Your response?

question.6b: My face burns red and I want to leave immediately
question.6c: Time seems to stop and I can't react at all
question.6d: I apologize profusely and check everyone's feelings

question.7a: The world won't leave me alone — I'm always ready to fight
question.7b: I want to escape to somewhere far away from here

fight.name: Fight Response
fight.tagline: A warrior who never backs down from threat
fight.description: Your nervous system switches to combat mode the moment it detects a threat. This powerful survival strategy developed in childhood to protect yourself. You have strong willpower and leadership, but sometimes anger becomes a mask for control and defense. True strength comes from allowing vulnerability.
fight.tip: Explore the emotions hiding behind your anger. Anger is often a shield for fear, sadness, or hurt. Ask yourself: 'Am I really angry right now, or am I scared?'

flight.name: Flight Response
flight.tagline: A survivor who instinctively runs from danger
flight.description: Your nervous system switches to escape mode the moment it detects a threat. This was a crucial strategy that kept you safe in the past. Behind your high productivity and constant activity, there may be an unconscious pattern of avoiding uncomfortable emotions. Stopping is also courage.
flight.tip: Notice the avoidance hidden behind your busyness. Try spending just 5 minutes a day doing absolutely nothing. Discomfort isn't a danger signal — it's the starting point of healing.

freeze.name: Freeze Response
freeze.description: Your nervous system shifts into shutdown mode when the threat feels too overwhelming. This is a natural response to protect yourself from what feels unbearable. Behind the numbness and dissociation, unprocessed emotions are safely waiting. You can start by feeling small things again.
freeze.tip: Reconnect with small sensations. Dip your hands in warm water or hold an ice cube. Reclaiming your body's sensations is the first step out of freeze.

fawn.name: Fawn Response
fawn.tagline: A harmonizer who surrenders self to avoid conflict
fawn.description: Your nervous system switches to appease-and-please mode when it detects a threat. This clever survival strategy developed in environments where conflict was dangerous. Behind your excellent empathy and relationship skills may hide a fear of losing your 'real self.' Your needs matter too.
fawn.tip: Practice one small 'no' every day. Saying no isn't rejecting the other person — it's choosing yourself. Start by asking: 'What do I actually want?'
